skills.name: aswath-compact
skills.description: Use when the session's context is filling, before a long task, or when the user says "compact", "free up context", "too much in context", or asks how much context is being used. Measures what the session is actually carrying, distils it into a dense handoff file, persists that handoff so any later session can resume from it, and reports how to actually release the window.

skills.name: aswath-token-evaluator
skills.description: Use when the user asks how many tokens a session used, what the context was spent on, how much was saved, whether the token guard is working, or wants a statistics report after a session. Produces a per-session table and a cause breakdown from the usage objects the runtime reports.

skills.name: aswath-token-guard
skills.description: Use when the user asks why a session is expensive, how much context is being used, what is wasting tokens, where the context window went, or before a long task that would grow the window. Measures the live session, attributes every token to a cause, names the largest waste, and applies the four habits that cut it. Also the entry point when a PreToolUse hook blocks a repeat read.

skills.name: aswath-token-ledger
skills.description: Use when the user wants the raw context ledger of a session - every token attributed to a cause, the costliest tool outputs, files read more than once - or wants to compare token spend across sessions. Reads the Claude Code and MiniMax Code transcript stores directly, including sessions that predate any hook.

skills.name: aswath-minimax-compaction-handoff
skills.description: Use when asked to set up, install, verify, or debug automatic context compaction for the MiniMax Code runtime, the 100k compaction trigger, HANDOFF.md generation before compaction using the context-compression structure (Session Intent, Files Modified, Decisions Made, Current State, Next Steps), or the PreCompact/PostCompact/SessionStart hook wiring in MiniMax Code.

skills.name: aswath-capability
skills.description: Orchestrator that takes a whole project from a one-line brief to shipped work. Use for 'build me an ecommerce site', 'build a project', 'I want to build X', 'start a project', or any end-to-end build that spans UI, architecture, and execution. It brainstorms the brief with you, researches whether the idea will actually work, plans UI and architecture, then resolves and invokes the right skills, subagents, hooks, MCPs and plugins from the registry - authoring missing ones mid-build when a real gap appears. Also use to run a UI design pass, a roast-and-fix cycle, or to discover what skills exist in the marketplace for a need.

skills.name: aswath-manual-demo
skills.description: Use when you want to see how a hand-written skill is captured into the shared catalog

skills.name: aswath-publish-github
skills.description: Use when creating a GitHub repository, pushing a project, opening a pull request, cutting a release, or publishing a gist — including phrases like "push to GitHub", "create a repo", "open a PR", "make a release", or "publish this to GitHub".

skills.name: aswath-publish-instagram
skills.description: Use when publishing, scheduling, or checking Instagram posts, reels, carousels, or stories from an AI agent — including phrases like "post to Instagram", "publish a reel", "share this carousel on Instagram", or any task naming Instagram as the destination.

skills.name: aswath-publish-linkedin
skills.description: Use when publishing, scheduling, deleting, or checking LinkedIn posts from an AI agent — including phrases like "post to LinkedIn", "share on LinkedIn", "publish my update", "check my LinkedIn posts", or any task naming LinkedIn as the destination.

skills.name: aswath-csvjson
skills.description: Use when converting CSV files to JSON, or when adding a CSV-to-JSON command to an existing tool

skills.name: aswath-catalog
skills.description: Use when a skill is in the wrong place, when two copies of a skill exist, when the published catalogue and the machine disagree, when a skill was edited in one place and did not change in another, or when the two PCs need to agree on what is installed. Also the entry point for "where is this skill actually", "which copy is the real one", and "check the skill layout".

skills.name: aswath-schedule
skills.description: Use when work should run without a human - the learning loop, the catalogue check, a job that must run late rather than never, or when the machine's scheduled jobs need seeing. Creates and removes Windows Task Scheduler jobs named Aswath\<name>, reports the Claude Code task list and the MiniMax cron table in one place, and marks the dead one-shots.

skills.name: aswath-chronicle
skills.description: Use when building features, refactoring, or making non-trivial decisions that require a persistent audit trail of user prompts, agent choices, and git history without wasting LLM tokens.

skills.name: aswath-commit
skills.description: Use when a change set is ready to commit and the reasoning must be written down. Produces a decision log and a file-by-file change inventory, then commits. No mass dumps.

skills.name: aswath-commit-discipline
skills.description: Use when work is about to be committed or pushed to GitHub, when the user says "push to GitHub", "mass push", "commit per meaningful work", "well documented commit", or when a change set needs its decisions, edits, prompts and new skills written down before it leaves the machine. Enforces the standing rule that every decision spoken with an AI, every edit, every prompt and every skill added is documented in detail and then committed and pushed, and that a brief with separable parts lands as one commit and one push per unit planned in docs/reviews/delivery-plan.md. The commit count is free; the detail is not.

skills.name: aswath-delivery
skills.description: Use when finished work goes back to a person on a chat channel - WhatsApp above all - and the chat must hold only the final version. Purges the superseded messages and files, sends the current build once, and leaves one clean final state.

skills.name: aswath-record
skills.description: Use when something ran and what it produced has to be written down - a build, a delivery, a failure - or when a secret may have reached a commit. Keeps the run and artifact ledger in the private store, reports the metrics, and checks that no secret file is tracked by git.

skills.name: aswath-improve
skills.description: Use when a skill keeps failing and should change itself - the run ledger holds a failure with no later success, and the change has to reach the published repo without a human in the middle. Writes the diff, opens the pull request, runs the gate, merges when the gate is green, and reverts the merge when the check after it fails.

skills.name: aswath-first-principles
skills.description: Use when a new project, feature, or build task has no approved spec yet, and the work would otherwise start from assumptions

skills.name: aswath-forge
skills.description: Use when starting any task that may already have a minted skill for it, or when a task needs a spec before any code is written

skills.name: aswath-thevai
skills.description: Use when a real person is the source of the brief — someone asks Aswath for a case study, deck, report, project or writeup and the requirement is not yet known. Collects the requirement from that person over WhatsApp instead of from assumptions: a warm, short conversation that ends in a brief they approved, then hands off to the build. Triggers: \"ask <name> what they want\", \"collect requirements\", \"thevai\", \"what does <name> actually need\", \"brief <name> on <topic>\".

skills.name: aswath-thinking
skills.description: Use when approaching non-trivial architecture problems, ungrounded prompts, or complex decision trade-offs before any code is written

skills.name: aswath-throw
skills.description: Use when the owner hands over a raw request, idea, or build-this and wants it executed end to end without hand-holding - the request is turned into a harness work item, gated by a leader-authored test, run by the agent pool, checked by two independent verifiers (one adversarial), projected for time, and reported back when it closes.

skills.name: aswath-talk
skills.description: [simple] How Aswath wants replies written — plain words, short sentences, no jargon walls, minimal ceremony, plus the "smallest thing that actually works" pushback. Use when the user says "aswath-talk", "talk like me", "plain english", "simpler", "too long", "i dont understand", or when a reply needs to be short and readable instead of dense. Combines caveman-style compression with ponytail-style minimalism and everyday wording.
